title: Plan change to rebuild fire-destroyed neighborhood
summary: The planning department proposed a plan change so homes lost in the August 8, 2023 fire can be rebuilt, and the commission recommended it with five votes, sending it to the County Council. The neighborhood's coastal permit will come back to the commission, and the homeowners association said delays mean months of extra rent for owners.

timeline.text: The special management area permit for the neighborhood will come back to the commission for a consistency finding.
The commission's motion to recommend the amendment passed with five votes.
The homeowners association said the delay means six extra months of high rent on top of mortgages for owners of destroyed homes.
The department plans to send the recommendation to the County Council, probably next week.
The governor's 18th emergency proclamation lets the planning director waive the special management area permit (a coastal permit) only temporarily.
The fire destroyed one single-family home and four multifamily buildings in the neighborhood.
The plan's specific park requirements for the area were added by the County Council, not recommended by the commission.
The planning department proposed a plan change so homes lost in the August 8, 2023 fire can be rebuilt.
